To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of soil water content measurements in a representative depth as basis for irrigation management can be an efficient and economical alternative to the common practice of using soil water potential measurements.
a modified approach based on sensor pairs is an efficient and economic alternative to determine soil water thresholds for irrigation control.
soil water content sensors are preferable to soil matric potential probes for irrigation management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
soil water monitoring in vineyards and the assessment of unsaturated soil hydraulic parameters as thresholds in irrigation management.
the practical use of soil water monitoring in a viticultural context.
the development and validation of a new approach for the determination of thresholds for irrigation control in vineyards.

the use of soil water content measurements in combination with a single sensor for the determination of the water content at field capacity can be a practical and economic alternative for irrigation control in vineyards.
